To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HMGB1 and TLR4 are required for the efficacy of conventional cancer treatments.
HMGB1 is an immunoadjuvants that promotes tumor-specific T-cell immunity and that HMGB1-dependent immunostimulatory pathways contribute to the success of conventional cancer treatment.

HMGB1 and TLR4 are critical mediators of the anticancer immune response triggered by cytotoxic treatments and that the genetic variation of TLR4 is a prognostic marker for breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular interactions between dying tumor and host cells that determine the efficacy of anticancer therapies.
the identification of molecular interactions that determine the outcome of conventional cancer treatment.
the identification of novel immunotherapeutic approaches to increase the efficacy of conventional cancer therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HMGB1 released from dying tumor cell is an important determinant of the efficacy of cytotoxic treatments in the context of cancer immunotherapy.
the HMGB1-TLR4 pathway is a critical component of the anticancer immunity induced by conventional cancer treatment.
TLR4 is a key player in the crosspresentation of cancer cell antigens by DCs, and that TLR4 polymorphisms may affect the outcome of chemotherapy in cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HMGB1 released by dying cancer cells can be used as a biomarker for the prognosis of cancer patients and as a target molecule for the design of new anticancer therapies.
the immunoadjuvant activity of tumor cell death is required to achieve a durable response to anticancer therapies.
HMGB1 released from dying tumor or stromal cells interacts with TLR4 on dendritic cells and promotes the crosspresentation of cancer-specific antigen to CD8+ T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficacy of anticancer therapies should be evaluated by considering not only the direct effects of cytotoxic treatments on tumor cells, but also their capacity to induce an effective immunoadjuvant response.
the immunoadjuvant effect of anticancer therapies should be considered when assessing their therapeutic potential.
the efficacy of conventional therapies is determined by the interplay between dying tumor cells, innate immune cells, and adaptive immunity.
